Apogee.label: Apogee
Apogee.tooltip: Highest altitude in the orbit, above the equatorial radius (6378.137 km)
Apogee.help: The highest point of the orbit, given as altitude above the Earth.

Perigee.label: Perigee
Perigee.tooltip: Lowest altitude in the orbit, above the equatorial radius (6378.137 km)
Perigee.help: The lowest point of the orbit, given as altitude above the Earth.

Inclination.label: Inclination
Inclination.tooltip: Angle Measured from Equator on the Ascending Node
Inclination.help: How far the orbit is tilted from the equator. 0° circles the equator; 90° passes over the poles.

Eccentricity.label: Eccentricity
Eccentricity.tooltip: How Circular the Orbit Is (0 is a Circle)
Eccentricity.help: How stretched the orbit is. 0 is a perfect circle; values near 1 are long ovals.

RightAsc.label: Right Asc.
RightAsc.tooltip: Where it Rises Above the Equator
RightAsc.help: Right ascension of the ascending node: the direction in the sky where the orbit crosses the equator heading north.

ArgOfPerigee.label: Arg of Perigee
ArgOfPerigee.tooltip: Where the Lowest Part of the Orbit Is
ArgOfPerigee.help: Argument of perigee: the angle along the orbit from that equator crossing to the lowest point.

Region.label: Over
Region.tooltip: Country under the sub-satellite point (Natural Earth borders)

Period.label: Period
Period.tooltip: Time for One Complete Revolution Around Earth
Period.help: How long the object takes to go around the Earth once.

Velocity.label: Velocity
Velocity.tooltip: Current Velocity of the Satellite (Higher the Closer to Earth it Is)

GPEpoch.label: GP Epoch
GPEpoch.tooltip: Epoch of the element set used for propagation

AgeOfGP.label: Age of GP
AgeOfGP.tooltip: Time from the GP epoch to the current simulation time (older GP data is usually less accurate; negative means the epoch is after the sim time)
AgeOfGP.epochAfterSimTime: GP epoch is after sim time

RadialSigma.label: Radial Sigma
RadialSigma.tooltip: 1-sigma radial position uncertainty from the TLE-derived covariance at the GP epoch (RIC frame). Same values Pc and the Conjunction Report use.

InTrackSigma.label: In Track Sigma
InTrackSigma.tooltip: 1-sigma in-track position uncertainty from the TLE-derived covariance at the GP epoch (RIC frame). Same values Pc and the Conjunction Report use.

CrossTrackSigma.label: Cross Track Sigma
CrossTrackSigma.tooltip: 1-sigma cross-track position uncertainty from the TLE-derived covariance at the GP epoch (RIC frame). Same values Pc and the Conjunction Report use.

CenterBody.label: Center Body
CenterBody.tooltip: Body the ephemeris positions are measured from (OEM CENTER_NAME)

RefFrame.label: Reference Frame
RefFrame.tooltip: Coordinate frame of the ephemeris (OEM REF_FRAME)

Regime.label: Regime
Regime.tooltip: The altitude band of the orbit
Regime.help: The altitude band of the orbit. LEO: low Earth orbit, under 2,000 km. MEO: medium Earth orbit, up to geostationary height. GEO: about 35,786 km over the equator, where an object stays over one spot. HEO: highly elliptical, or higher than GEO.
